transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-01 10:00 PT | Duration: ~60 minutes | Attendees: Samira, Michael, Jared, Lena, Priya, Ethan + all employees

00:00 Samira: Hey everybody, uh good morning, good afternoon depending where you are. Welcome to the Redwood June all-hands. We'll run about an hour, we'll cover Q2 highlights, product updates, hiring, and then leave time for Q&A. Quick ground rules, chat for questions, and we'll take some live mics toward the end.

00:28 Michael: Thanks Samira. Quick ops note, our Dedicated beta is at 75% of the customers in the pilot and latency SLOs are holding — median p95 token latency at 12 ms on rtx nodes, uh on the new runtime path. There's still some tail variance on long-sequence inference, we're tracking that with the kernel selection changes.

00:56 Jared: On product - Optimize is out of the internal preview, we'll be starting customer trials next week. The toolbox will suggest batching and quantization configs by workload, and there's a UI hook to preview unit-cost impact. Demo later in the week.

01:18 Lena: Engineering highlight: we shipped multi-tenant KV cache isolation for Dedicated pools, this reduces inter-tenant cache pollution and improves cold-start performance. Note: there were some mis-keys in the first rollout — we rolled back a few nodes last night and patched the allocator.

01:40 Samira: Nice. Quick numbers: ARR growth this quarter +28% quarter-over-quarter. Net retention is 110% driven by expansions from two mid-market customers. Sales, Priya?

01:55 Priya: Yup, we closed three new customers on Dedicated trials, and a large enterprise in finance signed up for a Private deployment evaluation — they'll be testing our VPC + KMS integration. We'll need sales+security sync after this.

02:18 Ethan: Security update: SOC 2 Type 1 is complete, Type 2 run starts next week. We also completed an initial HSM integration for key rotation; audit logs are now streaming to our SIEM. We'll add a compliance FAQ to the sales playbook.

02:40 Jared: On the roadmap, Private GA is still on track for late Q3. We're finalizing onboarding flows for customer-managed networking and a simplified install script for on-prem boxes. There's a remaining risk around third-party driver compatibility on older GPU vendors — we'll be sending a compatibility matrix.

03:05 Audience (Employee 1): Quick question — how are we measuring production quality when customers use quantized models? Are we tying evals to rollout?

03:18 Michael: Good Q. Yes, Optimize ties quality regression alerts to the eval sets, we have thresholding for model drift and per-prompt checks. If a quantized variant drops below our threshold we automatically tag the rollout and can fallback to a higher-precision variant. That path is a little noisy right now for rare long-tail prompts, which is a known item.

03:45 Samira: Hiring: we're planning to hire ~18 people this quarter across infra, SE, and product. Lena, any color on priorities?

03:55 Lena: Focus on infra (runtime performance), two senior kernel engineers, three backend, and two SEs for Dedicated onboarding. Also a headcount for a privacy/compliance engineer. We're pairing interviews with a coding + system design loop.

04:18 Audience (Employee 2): Anything on pricing changes for Hosted API? Customers are asking re: unit cost as token volumes go up.

04:30 Priya: No immediate list-price changes. We're introducing more granular reserved capacity tiers and custom billing for high-volume customers — aim is to give cheaper committed price for Dedicated while keeping hosted flexible.

04:50 Michael: Technical deep dive snippet — we've improved kernel scheduling by adding a dynamic sequence-length predictor that lets us pick shorter-kernel paths for 95% of traffic, that reduces average token compute by ~14% in our tests. Implementation is in the opt-kernel branch.

05:15 Samira: Quick shoutouts: CS team hit a big renewal this month, and engineering hit 98% test coverage on the runtime smoke tests.

05:35 Open Q&A and live mics.

06:00 Employee 3 (mike-ish): Are we comfortable with multi-region fallbacks if a region hits capacity during peak — will apps automatically failover?

06:18 Michael: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variants in other regions, but there is some added latency — we have a policy engine to prefer same-region then cross-region. We're working on predictive re-routing to reduce cold starts.

06:45 Employee 4: Any update on marketplace partnerships?

06:55 Priya: We're in talks with two cloud marketplaces for listing Dedicated SKUs, goal is Q4. Also partnership with a systems integrator for finance vertical.

07:15 Samira: Okay final reminders — exec offsite in July, submit session topics; we'll send out slides and recording. Thanks everyone, enjoy the rest of your day.

07:30 Meeting end. Recording and slides: link shared in follow-up (internal).

Notes on transcript: auto-generated, some words mis-transcribed (e.g., 'KV cache' sometimes read as 'K V cash'), occasional filler words (uh, you know).
